stories.title: EU renewable energy share, 2030 target
stories.then: The 2018 Renewable Energy Directive originally set a binding EU renewable-energy share target of at least 32% by 2030. This was a policy target, not a prediction that 32% would be achieved.
stories.now: The 2030 binding target was raised to at least 42.5% in 2023. Eurostat reported a 25.2% renewables share of EU gross final energy consumption for 2024, leaving a 17.3-percentage-point gap to the revised 2030 target.
stories.take: Progress observed; 2030 target not yet due; no claim of final realization.

progress_meter.label: Target-level yardstick (NOT a hindsight grade)
progress_meter.metric: 2024 renewable-energy share compared with the revised 2030 EU share target
progress_meter.note: Compares two levels; not a score for planning quality or a measure of percentage-point progress.

sources.finding: Directive revision raises target to at least 42.5%

stories.title: EU net greenhouse gas reduction toward 2030
stories.then: The EU policy objective is to reduce net greenhouse gas emissions by at least 55% by 2030 relative to 1990, and become climate neutral by 2050. These are targets, not predictions.
stories.now: The European Commission reported that provisional EU net greenhouse gas emissions in 2024 were 37.2% below 1990, within the scope of the EU climate target. The 2030 objective is not yet due.
stories.take: Observed emissions reductions; 2030 and 2050 objectives not yet verifiable as completed.

progress_meter.label: Target-level yardstick (NOT a hindsight grade)
progress_meter.metric: 2024 net-emissions reduction compared with the EU 2030 reduction goal, both versus 1990
progress_meter.note: A snapshot of the reduction versus the stated target, not a forecast-accuracy grade.

sources.finding: European Commission 2025 progress report gives 2024 net emissions reduction of 37.2% versus 1990
EEA says 2024 estimated net GHG emissions 37% below 1990; 55% 2030 goal not yet due

reading_shelf.title: Record dry summer in 2015 challenges precipitation projections in Central Europe
reading_shelf.then: In 2016, a study questioned how confidently climate projections describe Central Europe’s summers.
reading_shelf.later: A related 2018 modeling paper found very different possible summer-rainfall futures: wet, dry and very dry.
reading_shelf.take: This is later academic discussion, not a real-world test or proof that the earlier scenario happened.
reading_shelf.later_title: Varying soil moisture–atmosphere feedbacks explain divergent temperature extremes and precipitation projections in central Europe

scoring_note: Only an original-source-reviewed prediction with comparable independent outcome evidence can receive a hindsight grade.
